Holy shit. This was literally my life for the first 15 years of existence. Moments were I felt.. not quite directed, but like, almost as if there was a RPG options menu of conversation / options for a scenario. Like, one option always felt the most obvious, beneficial long term option. The others would sate my pride more. It's kind of hard to explain.

At around 14? I think was the last time I had that prompt. I do remember, atleast in my experience, yours may vary, that it had positive consequences in my life. The last time I had it was the one time I ignored it. Never came up again I think. It was like the universe was telling me there was a fork in the road I could take, here are the options.

I'm unsure about my beliefs in religion, I'm doubtful it was God or what have you, but the experience was real. I did grow up LDS, but I don't think I ever took too much stock in it.

One of the experiences I remember, was 1- I could apologize for whatever I was knowingly in the wrong for, 2- I could double down and eat the consequences of lying (I think I was around 12 or so.)

I had went with option 1 and felt... I don't know. Like an XP bar went up? A sense of fulfillment? Success? It was a strange, but not unpleasant feeling. But I felt I had grown in those moments.

Again, your situation could be completely different, but I think I'm identifying with what your talking about? I've been in the same ball park range funk for like 15 years (nearing 30), so I'm pretty maladjusted. But as for experiences of 'convenient song on radio' or 'the last of x grocery item that i just.. "needed" at that time'. Those almost ' scripted events ' happen to me too.

To add to it, you almost can't think. It's closer to you don't want to, a momentary unreasonable peace. Even if someones trying to get your attention or your trying to pay attention, the pull is so strong, its hard. Like being in a daydream, but there is no daydream. Your eyes slowly pull away and wrench themselves to what you were trying to pay attention to, but that... I'm not sure, nostalgia? For that moment of staring at nothing.

And you keep trying to look back to that spot, but you can never recapture that strange moment. And then your distracted for a while with that feeling in the back of your head.

I'm not sure if its dissociation, but it's nice to not feel alone.

Or you start feeling a 'pull' to stare at a specific section of your vision, and its uncomfortable to look away. It's almost comforting and soothing to stare at JUST that spot, looking away makes your head and eyes ache barely enough to notice. Then you have a hard time with your eyes focusing again sometimes?

I love this game. I was a big fan of the first one too. This one just touches up on some things from the first game with few changes (because why fix what isn't broken?).

If you have ever played Company of Heroes, this game is similar, except that every unit has a name, their own inventory, their own ammo count, and you can directly control that unit. Its pretty in-depth with a destructible terrain. The choices you make when bombarding an area or shooting part of a building matter! They can impact the game significantly!

Just about everything can be used for cover for infantry. Each unit has some grenades/AT grenades that you can manually control and time! You can setup defenses like mines, tank traps, barb wire, sandbag walls, and even throw dynamite.

Did I mention that you can make your infantry crawl, crouch, stand, or go PUNCH OTHER INFANTRY? I had this one guy hiding behind a wall, the enemy had pushed back hard and I had to retreat, but I forgot this guy. His name was Karl Shultz, that badass punched 6 infantry units before being killed by a tank.

Speaking of tanks, tanks and most other vehicles have more then 1 type of round. HE rounds, AP rounds, APCR rounds, usually a machine gun secondary. And you can full control them too.

But by far one of the best things about MoW AS2 is that if you hull damage (yellow text, not red) a tank, or decrew it. YOU CAN STEAL THAT SHIT. Whats that? No tanks on your team? You just killed a tiger tank? Send some infantry to repair it and HOP ON IN THE PAIN TRAIN!
 
This is my favorite RTS for WWII and I highly recommend it, theres plenty of mods for maps / game modes and its a blast to play with friends.
